name: BURUNDI

flag.title: Flag of Burundi
flag.note: Red & green split by white saltire + 3 stars

lead: Burundi is a tiny landlocked country in East Africa where green ridges drop to Lake Tanganyika — one of the world's deepest lakes. Called the Switzerland of Africa for its cool highlands, it is a land of thunderous royal drums, champion runners, and remarkable human energy packed into one of the continent's smallest countries.

sections.geography: A land of a thousand hills

geo: Burundi sits on a high plateau averaging 1,500 m above sea level, so even this tropical country feels pleasantly breezy. Forested ridges ripple east to west, broken by river valleys where banana plants crowd every slope.

Lake Tanganyika hugs the entire western edge: 676 km long and 1,471 m deep, with fish found nowhere else on Earth. A tiny stream on Mount Gikizi in the southern highlands is the most remote source of the River Nile.
animals: Kibira National Park in the northwest is Burundi's wildest corner — 400 km² of montane rainforest echoing with chimpanzee calls at dawn. Colobus monkeys leap through the canopy while hundreds of bird species dart through the mist.
Hippos wallow in the Rusizi River delta and along Lake Tanganyika's shore. Beneath the lake, over 130 species of cichlid fish shimmer in colours scientists study as a living masterclass in evolution.
culture: Burundi's heartbeat is the ingoma drum. Royal drummers — dressed in red, white and green — beat enormous hand-carved drums in perfect unison while dancing acrobatically. UNESCO added this tradition to its Intangible Heritage list in 2014.

Everyday life revolves around hillside farms growing plantains, sweet potatoes and sorghum. Friends sip urwagwa — a lightly fizzy banana beer — through long shared straws from a communal pot, a custom as old as the kingdom itself.
history: For centuries Burundi was a powerful monarchy; a mwami (king) was said to 'ascend the drum' when he took the throne. The kingdom survived Arab traders and German colonisers before Belgium took control after World War I.
Independence came on 1 July 1962. Painful civil conflict followed in later decades, but a peace deal in 2000 slowly rebuilt stability, and today a young population is shaping a new future.
wows: Burundi's flag has a saltire — a rare diagonal cross — dividing its red and green fields.
A spring in southern Burundi on Mount Gikizi is the most remote source of the River Nile.
Vénuste Niyongabo won Burundi's first Olympic gold at Atlanta 1996 in the 5,000 m race.
Lake Tanganyika holds 17% of Earth's unfrozen fresh surface water — second deepest lake on Earth.
Burundi is Africa's third most densely populated country — twice as crowded per km² as France.
Scientists rediscovered the Bururi long-fingered frog in 2011 — presumed extinct since 1949.
Gishora Sanctuary has two sacred drums so holy they have never once been struck.

myths.myth: Burundi and Rwanda are the same country
myths.fact: They are two entirely separate nations with their own governments, capitals and flags, though they share related languages and many cultural traditions.

myths.myth: Burundi has no wildlife because it’s so small
myths.fact: Kibira National Park shelters chimpanzees and 200+ bird species; Lake Tanganyika is a global hotspot for freshwater fish biodiversity.
